channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Digital fund worth £670m less than thought
item.description: The confirmed budget of NHS England’s flagship tech investment programme is £670m less than estimates given in the spring, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: Patients face risk of harm as hospital group splits
item.description: Details of the serious concerns raised by the Care Quality Commission about the collapsing Humber Health Partnership hospital group have been uncovered by HSJ.

item.title: Public inquiries a costly ‘knee jerk’, warns chair
item.description: The chair of a major public inquiry has admitted they are often “hugely expensive”, time-consuming, and popular with politicians who are keen to pass the buck to the next minister.

item.title: Ex-minister would sack half of managers he has met ‘in a heartbeat’
item.description: An ex-health minister has said he would sack half of the NHS managers he has met “in a heartbeat” for not being good enough.

item.title: HSJ Patient Safety Awards 2026: Winners revealed
item.description: The winners of the HSJ Patient Safety Awards 2026 were announced last night, recognising outstanding efforts to make care safer.

item.title: Safety leaders ‘battling challenging political narrative’
item.description: NHS England’s patient safety chief has said the service is having to “battle against a narrative” that it has not improved safety.

item.title: Urgent warning issued over cardiac death risk
item.description: A coroner has issued an urgent warning that the failure to implement an emergency cardiac pathway could result in more deaths.

item.title: Trusts name new CEO after group split
item.description: A hospital group has appointed a new chief executive a month after its wider group, with a neighbouring trust, unravelled.

item.title: Questions over ‘redundancy’ for second former ICB CEO
item.description: Questions have been raised over a second integrated care board CEO’s departure, after NHS England said they had been subject to compulsory redundancy despite this not being disclosed in accounts.

item.title: Closure of birthing units announced by ICBs
item.description: An integrated care board cluster has confirmed it will permanently close two birthing units.

item.title: ‘Summary dismissal’ warning for record snoopers
item.description: Staff facing a case to answer for snooping on patient records should be rapidly suspended, and “summary dismissal” will “usually” be appropriate for those found guilty, NHS England has said.

item.title: Doctor to chair trust after boardroom row
item.description: A clinical oncologist has been appointed to chair a trust whose previous chair quit after a draft investigation found she had “exceeded her authority” in suspending its chief executive.

item.title: NHS in ‘tight’ spot ahead of winter says NHSE CEO
item.description: The NHS England CEO has told HSJ the NHS is in a “tight” spot on emergency care ahead of winter, after performance took a major hit during the summer.

item.title: Mackey: Government should not take NHS recovery for granted
item.description: Performance and financial improvement remain “finely balanced” New ministers want focus on results for population groups, over provider models Treasury still “churning [us] up in pointless process” rather than giving the NHS “space” The Andy Burnham government must be careful not to assume recent improvements in NHS care ...

item.title: CEO who left for Gibraltar joins struggling trust
item.description: A leading trust chief executive who left the NHS to run Gibraltar’s health system has returned as an interim appointment at one of England’s largest providers.

item.title: Smallest trust to get managing director within group structure
item.description: England’s smallest trust will have its own managing director and dedicated deputy chair as it transitions into a group model with two other providers.

item.title: ‘Angry’ trust CEO warns staff about racist abuse of director
item.description: The chief people officer of a leading hospital trust has been subjected to “racist” abuse by colleagues, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Accounting error forces trust to downgrade forecast by £6m
item.description: The NHS’s worst-performing mental health trust had to adjust its accounts to record a £2.9m deficit after external auditors found it had wrongly classified £6m as an efficiency saving.

item.title: Under-fire trust pauses CEO recruitment
item.description: A major trust under intense scrutiny over quality and governance concerns has paused its search for a permanent chief executive.

item.title: Keeping FT governors is pure virtue signalling, claims chair
item.description: The chair of one of the country’s largest foundation trusts has dismissed pledges by other FTs to keep their councils of governors as “virtue signalling”.
